title: Research method for Type 2 diabetes (T2D) predicted effector genes (Mahajan et al., 2022)
bodyHtml:
These results were generated in the study:

Multi-ancestry genetic study of type 2 diabetes highlights the power of diverse populations for discovery and translation.
Mahajan A, et al.
Nat Genet. 2022 May;54(5):560-572. doi: 10.1038/s41588-022-01058-3.
PMID: 35551307

The GWAS meta-analysis performed in this study (integrated into the Knowledge Portals as DIAMANTE 2022 T2D GWAS: trans-ancestry) included 180,834 individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and 1,159,055 controls. Annotation-informed multi-ancestry fine-mapping performed on the genome-wide association results identified distinct association signals within the loci associated with T2D at stringent genome-wide significance (p < 5e-9).

Bayesian colocalization was performed between the association signals and eQTLs from T2D-relevant tissues: pancreatic islet eQTLs from the InsPIRE Consortium (Viñuela et al., 2020) and subcutaneous adipose tissue, visceral adipose tissue, brain hypothalamus, liver, and skeletal muscle eQTLs from the GTEx Project. The table lists candidate effector genes at signals with posterior probability (πCOLOC) greater than 80%.
